instructions: Bihar STET Paper 2 Computer Science practice mock test.

questions.question: Which fopen mode opens a file for appending text?
questions.explanation: The a mode appends writes at the end, creating the file if permitted and absent.

questions.question: What does strlen("cat") return?
questions.explanation: strlen counts characters before the terminating null byte, so it returns 3.

questions.question: Clustering is usually an example of:
questions.explanation: Clustering groups data without supplied target labels.

questions.question: A full binary tree is one in which every node has:
questions.explanation: A full/proper binary tree has zero or two children at each node.

questions.question: A balanced binary search tree supports search in typical worst-case:
questions.explanation: A balanced BST has logarithmic height, so search is O(log n).

questions.question: Which keyword declares a block-scoped variable that can be reassigned?
questions.explanation: let declares a block-scoped variable that can be reassigned.

questions.question: Black-box testing derives tests primarily from:
questions.explanation: Black-box tests focus on specified inputs and observable outputs.

questions.question: An interrupt vector commonly identifies:

options.text: The address of an interrupt service routine

questions.explanation: An interrupt vector provides or identifies the handler address.

questions.question: The CIA triad stands for:
questions.explanation: CIA is confidentiality, integrity and availability.

questions.question: Dynamic binding determines the method implementation:

options.text: At runtime based on the actual object/type
At the time a comment is written

questions.explanation: Dynamic dispatch selects an overridden method based on runtime type.

questions.question: A priority queue removes an element according to:

options.text: Only insertion time in all implementations

questions.explanation: Priority queues select elements according to priority, with tie behavior implementation-dependent.

questions.question: A superkey may contain:

options.text: Extra attributes beyond a candidate key
No attribute at all in every relation

questions.explanation: A superkey uniquely identifies tuples but need not be minimal.

questions.question: BFS finds shortest paths in an unweighted graph in terms of:

options.text: Total edge weight for arbitrary weights

questions.explanation: BFS minimizes the number of edges in an unweighted graph.

questions.question: In a min-heap, the root contains:

options.text: A minimum key among the heap elements
The most recently inserted key always

questions.explanation: The min-heap property puts a minimum element at the root.

questions.question: Simplify A AND (A OR B):
questions.explanation: By absorption, A(A+B)=A.

questions.question: A full backup copies:

options.text: All selected data in the backup scope
Only changes since the last backup

questions.explanation: A full backup copies all selected data in its defined scope.

questions.question: How many times does for(i=0; i<4; i++) execute its body if it completes normally?
questions.explanation: The values of i are 0, 1, 2 and 3: four iterations.

questions.question: A 3-2-1 backup strategy commonly means keeping:

options.text: 3 copies, on 2 types of media, with 1 off-site

questions.explanation: The 3-2-1 rule promotes redundancy and an off-site copy.

questions.question: Which clause sorts query output?
questions.explanation: ORDER BY sorts the result rows.

questions.question: Insertion sort is particularly efficient on:

options.text: All reverse-sorted arrays with guaranteed O(n log n)
Unsorted linked data with no comparisons

questions.explanation: Insertion sort performs well for small or nearly sorted inputs, though worst case is O(n²).

questions.question: A median is:

options.text: The middle value after ordering observations
The sum divided by count in every case

questions.explanation: The median is the middle ordered observation, or average of two middles for even n.

questions.question: In C, the result of comparing two values with == is an integer value that is:
questions.explanation: Relational and equality operators yield int value 0 or 1.

questions.question: The ALU primarily performs:
questions.explanation: The arithmetic logic unit performs arithmetic and logical operations.

questions.question: Adjacent K-map cells differ in:
questions.explanation: Gray-code ordering makes adjacent cells differ in one variable.

questions.question: If ptr is a pointer to a structure, which expression accesses member x?
questions.explanation: The arrow operator accesses a member through a structure pointer.

questions.question: UTF-8 is a variable-length encoding for:
questions.explanation: UTF-8 encodes Unicode code points using one to four bytes.

questions.question: Edge computing processes data:

options.text: Near the device or data source
Only in a distant central cloud

questions.explanation: Edge computing reduces the need to send all processing to a central cloud.

questions.question: Which format commonly supports lossless compression and transparency?
questions.explanation: PNG supports lossless image compression and alpha transparency.

questions.question: What is the meaning of a null pointer?

options.text: It does not point to a valid object/function
It always points to address zero as a usable object
It points to the first array element
It is identical to every uninitialized pointer

questions.explanation: A null pointer is a distinguished pointer value that does not designate an object or function.

questions.question: Deleting a known node from a doubly linked list can be O(1) if:

options.text: Its neighboring links can be updated directly
The list must be sorted first
The entire list is searched regardless

questions.explanation: With a direct node reference, predecessor/successor links can be updated in constant time.

questions.question: A Turing machine's tape is used as:

options.text: An unbounded computational storage model in the standard abstraction

questions.explanation: The standard Turing machine model uses a tape as working storage.

questions.question: Virtual addresses are translated to physical addresses by hardware commonly involving the:
questions.explanation: The memory management unit performs address translation and protection checks.

questions.question: Which application naturally uses a stack?
questions.explanation: Function calls and returns use a call stack.

questions.question: The expression [x*x for x in range(4)] produces:
questions.explanation: range(4) gives 0,1,2,3 and each is squared.

questions.question: Isolation in ACID concerns:
questions.explanation: Isolation controls the visibility/interleaving of concurrent transaction operations.

questions.question: A TLB is a cache of:
questions.explanation: The translation lookaside buffer caches page-table translation information.

questions.question: A file extension is primarily used to suggest:

options.text: The file's physical location in RAM

questions.explanation: Extensions commonly indicate file formats, though they are not definitive proof.

questions.question: A firewall is used primarily to:

options.text: Filter network traffic according to security rules

questions.explanation: Firewalls permit or block traffic according to policy.

questions.question: Which storage device has no moving mechanical parts?
questions.explanation: SSDs use flash memory and have no spinning platters.

questions.question: A model that performs well on training data but poorly on unseen data may be:
questions.explanation: Overfitting means the model has not generalized well to unseen data.

questions.question: A PDA differs from a finite automaton mainly by having:
questions.explanation: A pushdown automaton has stack memory.

questions.question: Indexed file allocation stores file block pointers in:
questions.explanation: Indexed allocation maintains a block of pointers to a file's data blocks.

questions.question: What does a return statement do in a function?

options.text: Transfers control back to the caller, optionally with a value

questions.explanation: return exits the current function and may provide a return value.

questions.question: A NAND gate is equivalent to:

options.text: XOR followed by NOT only for unequal inputs

questions.explanation: NAND is the complement of AND.

questions.question: Backtracking solves a search problem by:

options.text: Building candidates and abandoning partial candidates that cannot work

questions.explanation: Backtracking prunes partial solutions that cannot lead to a valid solution.

questions.question: Which algorithm can cause starvation of low-priority processes if priorities are never adjusted?

options.text: Round Robin with equal time slices

questions.explanation: Low-priority processes may wait indefinitely under fixed priority scheduling.

questions.question: In a declaration int a[4][5], how many int elements are allocated?
questions.explanation: There are 4×5 = 20 elements.

questions.question: Conditional compilation can be controlled using:
questions.explanation: Preprocessor conditionals include #if, #ifdef and #endif.

questions.question: A use case typically describes:

options.text: An actor's interaction with a system to achieve a goal

questions.explanation: Use cases capture actor-system interactions toward goals.

questions.question: A decoder with n input bits can have up to how many output lines?
questions.explanation: An n-to-2ⁿ decoder can select one of 2ⁿ outputs.

questions.question: Which Python structure stores unique hashable elements without a guaranteed positional order?
questions.explanation: A set stores unique hashable elements; it is not an index-based sequence.

questions.question: Which keyword makes an object non-modifiable through that identifier?
questions.explanation: const-qualified objects are not modifiable through that qualified lvalue.

questions.question: A routing table is used to determine:

options.text: Where to forward packets toward destination networks

questions.explanation: Routing tables select next hops/interfaces for destination prefixes.

questions.question: Average-case lookup in a well-designed hash table is often:
questions.explanation: With a good hash function and controlled load factor, average lookup is constant time.

questions.question: Prim's algorithm finds a:
questions.explanation: Prim grows a minimum spanning tree in a connected weighted undirected graph.

questions.question: A /30 IPv4 prefix contains how many total addresses?
questions.explanation: A /30 leaves 2 host bits, giving 2² = 4 total addresses.

questions.question: An opcode specifies:
questions.explanation: Opcode bits identify the instruction operation.

questions.question: A critical section is a code region that accesses:

options.text: An isolated local variable in all cases

questions.explanation: Critical sections need synchronization when concurrent access could conflict.

questions.question: Which category includes exceptions that Java requires a method to catch or declare, excluding RuntimeException subclasses?
questions.explanation: Checked exceptions are subject to catch-or-declare rules.

questions.question: The degree of a vertex in an undirected graph is the number of:

options.text: Incident edges, counting a loop twice

questions.explanation: An undirected vertex's degree counts incident edges; a loop contributes two.

questions.question: Which SQL aggregate function counts rows?
questions.explanation: COUNT() returns the number of rows or non-NULL values depending on its argument.

questions.question: Maintainability refers to how easily software can be:

options.text: Modified to correct, improve or adapt it
Read only by its original author

questions.explanation: Maintainability concerns modification and evolution effort.

questions.question: Wi-Fi networks are based on the IEEE family:
questions.explanation: Wi-Fi standards belong to IEEE 802.11.

questions.question: An object is an instance of a:
questions.explanation: A class describes a type; an object is an instance of that class.

questions.question: ASCII was originally a character code based on:
questions.explanation: Original ASCII defines 128 code points using 7 bits.

questions.question: Open-source software generally allows users to:

options.text: Inspect, use and modify source under its license terms
Use it without any license conditions
Always sell it under any terms

questions.explanation: Open-source permissions are governed by the specific license.

questions.question: A constructor is mainly used to:
questions.explanation: Constructors establish an object's initial state.

questions.question: If T(n)=T(n/2)+O(1), the usual asymptotic time is:
questions.explanation: The input size halves each step, giving logarithmically many levels.

questions.question: Which protocol is connectionless at the transport layer?
questions.explanation: UDP sends datagrams without establishing a transport connection.

questions.question: In register addressing, the operand is located in:
questions.explanation: Register addressing specifies a register containing the operand.

questions.question: A /26 IPv4 subnet contains how many total addresses?
questions.explanation: A /26 leaves 6 host bits, giving 2⁶ = 64 total addresses.

questions.question: Which flip-flop toggles its output when its T input is 1 at the active clock edge?
questions.explanation: A T flip-flop toggles when T=1.

questions.question: Which attribute specifies the destination URL for a form submission?
questions.explanation: The form action attribute identifies the submission endpoint.

questions.question: The Singleton pattern aims to:

options.text: Ensure a class has one controlled instance
Create one object for every input byte

questions.explanation: Singleton restricts a class to one instance and provides a global access point.

questions.question: Merge sort is an example of:
questions.explanation: Merge sort splits, recursively sorts and merges subarrays.

questions.question: A cache hit occurs when:

options.text: The requested item is found in cache

questions.explanation: A cache hit means the needed item is present in the cache.

questions.question: A tuple in a relation corresponds most closely to a:
questions.explanation: A tuple is a row/record in a relation.

questions.question: Which component provides the user with a command-line interface?
questions.explanation: A shell interprets commands and provides an interface to OS services.

questions.question: A race condition occurs when the result depends on:
questions.explanation: Race conditions arise when concurrent execution order affects behavior.

questions.question: A version-control system primarily tracks:
questions.explanation: Version control records and manages changes to project files.

questions.question: A partial functional dependency is relevant to violation of:
questions.explanation: Second normal form removes partial dependencies of non-prime attributes on candidate keys.

questions.question: A shared lock is commonly compatible with:

options.text: Another shared lock on the same item
An exclusive lock on the same item in every protocol

questions.explanation: Shared locks usually permit concurrent readers while excluding conflicting writers.

questions.question: Which Java collection interface models a sequence that can contain duplicates?
questions.explanation: List is an ordered collection that can contain duplicates.

questions.question: A process waiting for an I/O event is commonly in the:
questions.explanation: A process waiting for an event is blocked until that event occurs.

questions.question: Logical data independence is the ability to change the conceptual schema without changing:

options.text: External views/application programs, subject to mappings

questions.explanation: Logical data independence isolates external views from conceptual-schema changes.

questions.question: In a context-free grammar, terminals represent:

options.text: Symbols of strings in the generated language

questions.explanation: Terminals are the alphabet symbols appearing in generated strings.

questions.question: An enum in C defines:

options.text: Named integer constants and an enumeration type

questions.explanation: Enumeration constants have integer values and form an enum type.

questions.question: A lexeme is:

options.text: The actual character sequence matching a token pattern

questions.explanation: A lexeme is the source text instance represented by a token.

questions.question: A hybrid cloud combines:

options.text: Only a laptop and a printer

questions.explanation: Hybrid cloud combines distinct environments, commonly private and public clouds.

questions.question: In 8-bit signed magnitude representation, the range is:
questions.explanation: One sign bit and seven magnitude bits give −127 through +127, with both +0 and −0.

questions.question: Which algorithm can handle negative edge weights but not reachable negative cycles for shortest-path results?
questions.explanation: Bellman–Ford supports negative weights and can detect negative cycles.

questions.question: Which grows fastest asymptotically as n increases?
questions.explanation: For sufficiently large n, n² grows faster than n log n, n and log n.

questions.question: External fragmentation occurs when free memory is:

options.text: Split into separated holes that may not satisfy a large request

questions.explanation: External fragmentation leaves free space in non-contiguous holes.

questions.question: SCAN disk scheduling is also commonly called the:
questions.explanation: SCAN moves the disk head in one direction servicing requests, then reverses.

questions.question: Ping commonly uses which protocol to test IP reachability?
questions.explanation: Ping commonly sends ICMP echo requests and receives echo replies.

questions.question: Symmetric encryption uses:

options.text: The same shared secret key for encryption and decryption
A different public key for every byte

questions.explanation: Symmetric schemes use a shared secret key.

questions.question: Programmed I/O typically requires the CPU to:

options.text: Poll or directly manage device status/data transfer

questions.explanation: In programmed I/O the CPU actively checks status and moves data.

questions.question: The regular expression a* denotes:

options.text: Zero or more repetitions of a

questions.explanation: Kleene star permits zero or more occurrences of a.

questions.question: Dead-code elimination removes code that:

options.text: Cannot affect observable program behavior under the analysis assumptions

questions.explanation: Dead code can be removed because it has no observable effect.

questions.question: Which protocol is commonly used to send outgoing email from a client to a mail server?
questions.explanation: SMTP is used for message submission/transfer.

questions.question: Cooperative learning differs from simply seating students in groups because it includes:

options.text: Structured positive interdependence and individual accountability

questions.explanation: Cooperative learning deliberately structures shared responsibility and individual contribution.

questions.question: The average of 12, 16, 20 and 24 is:
questions.explanation: The sum is 72; 72/4 = 18.

questions.question: A learner who needs more time on a task may benefit from:

options.text: Appropriate time adjustment and chunked instructions

questions.explanation: Adjustments can improve access while retaining the intended learning goal.

questions.question: Which file should you be most cautious about opening from an unexpected email?

options.text: A document you created yourself offline
A known school timetable from an official portal
A plain text note you requested

questions.explanation: Unexpected executable attachments can carry malware; verify the sender and context.

questions.question: Which activity best encourages analysis?

options.text: Compare two solutions and explain their strengths and limits
Copy a paragraph word for word

questions.explanation: Comparison with reasons requires analysis.

questions.question: When parents and teachers disagree, a constructive approach is to:

options.text: Listen to concerns and focus on evidence and shared learner goals

questions.explanation: Respectful dialogue around evidence supports joint problem-solving.

questions.question: Choose the odd one out:
questions.explanation: The Moon is a natural satellite; the others are planets.

questions.question: What is 35% of 200?
If 4 pens cost ₹52, what is the cost of 7 pens at the same rate?
questions.explanation: One pen costs ₹13; seven cost ₹91.

questions.question: The head of the elected Union government in India is the:
questions.explanation: The Prime Minister heads the Union Council of Ministers and government.

questions.question: A shopkeeper buys an item for ₹400 and sells it for ₹460. The profit percentage is:
Reasonable accommodation aims to:

options.text: Remove barriers so a learner can participate meaningfully

questions.explanation: Accommodations improve access without necessarily changing the core learning goal.

questions.question: To clarify a confusing instruction, a teacher should:

options.text: Restate it in simpler steps and check understanding

questions.explanation: Clear chunked instructions plus a check for understanding improve access.

questions.question: A respectful online discussion should:
questions.explanation: Respectful digital citizenship avoids harassment and protects privacy.

questions.question: A browser's private/incognito mode generally does NOT guarantee:

options.text: That the internet service provider or websites cannot observe activity
That local browsing history is not saved in the usual browser history
That a separate local session is used
That some local session data is cleared after closing

questions.explanation: Private mode limits local traces but does not make users invisible to websites or network providers.

questions.question: Composting is most suitable for many types of:
questions.explanation: Composting processes organic materials into a soil amendment.

questions.question: Which number does not fit: 11, 13, 17, 19, 21, 23?
questions.explanation: 21 is composite; the other numbers listed are prime.

questions.question: A learner gives a partially correct answer. The teacher's best response is to:

options.text: Acknowledge the valid part and ask a prompt to extend reasoning
Mark it wholly wrong without discussion
Tell the class the learner is weak

questions.explanation: Building on correct reasoning helps learners refine their understanding.

questions.question: A preventive classroom-management strategy is to:

options.text: Teach routines and expectations before problems arise
Wait for disruption before explaining any rules
Use sarcasm as the main response

questions.explanation: Explicit routines and expectations prevent avoidable disruption.

questions.question: A teacher can reduce domination in group discussion by:

options.text: Using turn-taking roles and inviting quieter members
Allowing one student to answer every time

questions.explanation: Structured turn-taking helps distribute participation.

questions.question: Which force pulls objects toward Earth?
questions.explanation: Gravity attracts objects with mass toward Earth.

questions.question: Which body audits the receipts and expenditure of the Union and state governments?

options.text: Comptroller and Auditor General of India

questions.explanation: The CAG audits government accounts under constitutional provisions.

questions.question: Which action helps reduce household electricity use?

options.text: Switch off unused lights and equipment
Keep every light on all day
Leave chargers and devices running unnecessarily

questions.explanation: Switching off unused devices reduces avoidable electricity consumption.

questions.question: Scaffolding refers to:

options.text: Temporary support gradually reduced as competence grows
Permanent completion of all tasks by the teacher

questions.explanation: Scaffolding provides support that is withdrawn as learners become more independent.

questions.question: A person walks 6 m south and then 8 m west. Straight-line distance from the start is:
questions.explanation: Distance = √(6²+8²)=10 m.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: 'Neither of the answers ___ correct.'
questions.explanation: In standard formal usage, 'neither' takes a singular verb here: is.

questions.question: A prerequisite check helps a teacher identify:

options.text: Prior knowledge needed for the new lesson

questions.explanation: Prerequisite checks reveal readiness and gaps in relevant prior knowledge.

questions.question: A teacher notices a colleague sharing student marks in a public group. A responsible response is to:

options.text: Follow school policy to address the privacy breach
Forward the message to more groups

questions.explanation: Student data should be protected and concerns handled through appropriate channels.

questions.question: Find the next term: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, __.
questions.explanation: These are squares 1², 2², 3², 4², 5²; next is 6²=36.

questions.question: When several learners misunderstand the same instruction, a teacher should:

options.text: Clarify the instruction and check understanding again
Change the grading scale without explanation

questions.explanation: A shared misunderstanding often calls for clearer directions and a follow-up check.

questions.question: The area of a rectangle 12 cm long and 5 cm wide is:
questions.explanation: Area = length × width = 12×5 = 60 cm².

questions.question: A train travels 240 km in 4 hours. Its average speed is:
All teachers are graduates. Some graduates are artists. Which must be true?
questions.explanation: Only the first statement is directly guaranteed by the premise.

questions.question: A student reports bullying. The teacher should first:

options.text: Listen, ensure immediate safety and follow safeguarding/reporting procedures
Promise to keep it secret under all circumstances

questions.explanation: Safety and established reporting procedures take priority.

questions.question: Offering learners meaningful choices within a task can support:
questions.explanation: Appropriate choice can support autonomy and motivation.

questions.question: An exit ticket is most commonly used as:

options.text: A brief formative check at the end of a lesson

questions.explanation: Exit tickets provide quick evidence of learning at lesson end.

questions.question: A useful professional learning goal should be:

options.text: Specific and connected to evidence of student learning

questions.explanation: Specific goals linked to evidence make professional learning actionable.

questions.question: Which planet is known for its prominent ring system?
questions.explanation: Saturn is especially known for its extensive rings.

questions.question: P is to the left of Q, and Q is to the left of R in a row facing north. Who is in the middle?
questions.explanation: The order is P, Q, R, so Q is in the middle.

questions.question: A diagnostic assessment is intended mainly to:

options.text: Identify strengths, gaps or misconceptions before targeted support

questions.explanation: Diagnostic assessment identifies specific learning needs.

questions.question: Giving students a short pause before asking for responses can:

options.text: Improve thinking time and broaden participation
Ensure no one needs to think

questions.explanation: Wait time gives learners a chance to formulate responses.

questions.question: If today is Friday, what day will it be 9 days later?
questions.explanation: 9 days is 7+2; Friday plus two days is Sunday.

questions.question: If EAST is coded as FBTU by shifting each letter one forward, WEST is coded as:
questions.explanation: W→X, E→F, S→T, T→U.

questions.question: If a learner struggles with place value, useful remediation should include:

options.text: Concrete materials and targeted place-value tasks

questions.explanation: Concrete representations and focused practice can address place-value misconceptions.

questions.question: The National Education Policy 2020 recommends a school structure commonly expressed as:
questions.explanation: NEP 2020 proposes the 5+3+3+4 curricular and pedagogical structure.

questions.question: Individual differences mean a teacher should expect learners to:

options.text: Vary in pace, interests and ways of demonstrating understanding
Develop at exactly the same rate
Need identical supports in every situation
Have fixed abilities that never change

questions.explanation: Learners differ, so instruction may need flexible support.

questions.question: A balanced diet should generally include:

options.text: A variety of nutrients in suitable proportions

questions.explanation: A balanced diet includes varied nutrients according to individual needs.

questions.question: Which is a likely effect of deforestation?

options.text: Habitat loss and increased soil erosion risk

questions.explanation: Removing forest cover can reduce habitat and expose soil to erosion.

questions.question: If a student cannot access an online learning platform at home, a teacher should:

options.text: Offer an accessible alternative and follow school support procedures
Post the student's private details online

questions.explanation: Equitable planning considers access constraints and provides appropriate alternatives.

questions.question: Reliability and validity are different because reliability concerns consistency while validity concerns:

options.text: Whether the assessment supports the intended interpretation/use
The font size of the paper

questions.explanation: Reliability is consistency; validity concerns the appropriateness of interpretations and uses.
